recommendations.title: Receipt Self-Hash Unverifiable — Recompute Before Commit
recommendations.detail: The identity_freeze_receipt.json claims SHA-256 '9ac2e924...' for itself, but this hash does not match under any tested canonical algorithm. The receipt also contradicts itself: integrity.receipt_self_reference says 'NONE' but frozen_artifacts.identity_freeze_receipt.sha256 IS a self-reference. Per NSEC Article 44, receipts must be independently verifiable and must exclude self-referencing fields. Recommendation: recompute the receipt hash after removing the self-referencing sha256 field, or wait for Git commit SHA to serve as the receipt's integrity anchor.
recommendations.action: Before committing to Git, recompute receipt SHA using canonical algorithm (sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) after removing frozen_artifacts.identity_freeze_receipt.sha256, then insert the correct computed value. The Git commit SHA will serve as the ultimate integrity anchor.

recommendations.title: Canonical Hash Algorithm Drift Between NSEC Article 44 and Report
recommendations.detail: NSEC Article 44 specifies the canonical algorithm as 'hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()' (no ensure_ascii parameter — defaults to True). The report (line 155) and receipt (line 156) specify 'sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False'. Both the contract and report hashes were computed with ensure_ascii=False and verified correctly. However, the algorithm stated in Article 44 (ensure_ascii=True, the Python default) would produce DIFFERENT hashes. This creates ambiguity about which algorithm future gates should use.
recommendations.action: Align the canonical algorithm specification: either update NSEC Article 44 to include ensure_ascii=False, or recompute all hashes with ensure_ascii=True (Python default). The former is recommended since ensure_ascii=False preserves Unicode characters in their native form.

recommendations.title: Add Receipt Self-Hash Verification Instruction
recommendations.detail: The receipt correctly documents the canonical hash algorithm and verification instruction (lines 154-158), but the instruction does not explicitly state that the receipt's own hash must be verified by excluding the self-referencing sha256 field. Adding this would prevent future confusion.
recommendations.action: Update integrity.verification_instruction to include: 'For this receipt: exclude frozen_artifacts.identity_freeze_receipt.sha256 before computing the receipt's own SHA-256, per Article 44 self-reference exclusion.'
